answer: The lotus counter is kept in quill and lantern makes public each reset. A hostile operator as a result has to keep each alias continuously active for 32 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. A bond is refunded only after 32 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. That bill is paid per identity, so 135 aliases cost 261 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
